question: What does a scale read in a falling lift?

scene.title: What does a scale read in a falling lift?
scene.subtitle: Stand on a bathroom scale in a lift, then imagine the cable snaps. The answer explains why astronauts float.
scene.why: It is why astronauts float and roller-coaster drops feel weightless, and it was the clue that led Einstein to his theory of gravity.
scene.opening: A lift’s cable snaps. What does the bathroom scale under your feet read as you fall?

beats.title: Standing still
beats.body: In a parked lift, the scale reads your weight. The floor pushes up on the scale, and the scale pushes up on you.

beats.title: Riding up and down
beats.body: When the lift speeds up upward, the floor has to push harder, so the scale reads more. When it slows down, it reads less. A scale measures how hard it is pushed, not gravity itself.

beats.title: The cable snaps
beats.body: Now the lift falls freely. You, the scale and the apple you let go of all fall together, so nothing has to push anything. The scale reads zero, and the apple stays beside you.

beats.title: Weightless, not gravity-free
beats.body: Gravity hasn’t switched off: the lift keeps falling faster and faster. It acts on everything inside equally, so nothing presses on anything. Astronauts float for the same reason: their station is always falling around the Earth.

scene.takeaway: A scale measures pushes, not gravity. In free fall nothing pushes, so you feel weightless while gravity is still there.

questions.q: Astronauts on the space station float. Is there no gravity up there?
questions.a: There is: about nine tenths as strong as on the ground. They float because they and their station are falling around the Earth together, so nothing pushes on them.

questions.q: A lift starts moving downward. Does the scale read more or less than your weight?
questions.a: Less, while the lift speeds up downward: the floor doesn’t need to push as hard. Once it moves at a steady speed, the reading is back to normal.

questions.q: You jump off a diving board with a small scale strapped under your feet. What does it read on the way down?
questions.a: Zero. You and the scale fall together, so nothing presses on it.
